claim: Within the linear no-flow leaky-aquifer model on a bounded Lipschitz domain, with time-independent uniformly elliptic symmetric transmissivity tensor \(\mathbf T(x)\), positive storage coefficient \(S(x)\), bounded leakance \(\lambda(x)\ge0\), zero initial drawdown, and pumping density \(q(x,t)\) whose total is \(Q(t)=\int_\Omega q(x,t)\,dx\), the aggregate leakage history is independent of transmissivity, domain geometry, and spatial pumping profile for every prescribed total pumping history if and only if \(\lambda(x)/S(x)=\kappa\ge0\) almost everywhere. In that case the total leakage rate is exactly \(\mathcal L(t)=\kappa\int_0^t e^{-\kappa(t-u)}Q(u)\,du\); for constant pumping \(Q\), it is \(\mathcal L(t)=Q(1-e^{-\kappa t})\).

correctness.rationale: The weak-form mass balance with test function 1 yields M′ = Q - L. If lambda/S = kappa, then L = kappa M and the exact scalar ODE gives the convolution formula. Necessity follows because L′(0+) = Q(0) integral[(lambda/S)w] for each normalized spatial source profile w; equality across all profiles forces lambda/S to be constant almost everywhere. The no-flow boundary, zero initial drawdown, linearity, and static coefficients are explicit.

evidence: Butler and Tsou (2003) present homogeneous Hantush-Jacob and stream-aquifer cases and demonstrate bounded-domain invariance with image-well arguments; their numerical rectangular examples use the same grid-cell count.

The current theorem allows arbitrary time-independent uniformly elliptic transmissivity, spatially varying storage and leakance satisfying lambda/S = kappa, and arbitrary nonnegative pumping histories.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The extension is broader in coefficient heterogeneity and forcing. The formula follows from a weak mass balance and does not depend on image-well representability or rectangular geometry. It does not extend to arbitrary lambda/S, aquitard storage dynamics, or nonzero lateral flux.

originality.rationale: The result is narrowly scoped to an iff characterization of source-profile independence and an arbitrary-schedule leakage transfer function under heterogeneous coefficients. Butler and Tsou (2003) establish homogeneous scale invariance and image-well arguments for representative geometries but do not state this coefficient characterization in the inspected full text. The literature search did not locate a directly covering published theorem. This is best-knowledge originality, not proof of global uniqueness.
residual_risks: The integrated mass-balance argument is elementary and may be implicit in standard groundwater texts not located by semantic search; originality is limited to the explicit iff coefficient criterion and arbitrary-schedule formulation.
The Hantush-Jacob primary paper was inspected only at abstract level, so it is not used to claim that its full text lacks an equivalent extension.
The theorem does not cover aquitard storage dynamics, nonzero lateral boundary flux, time-varying coefficients, nonlinear leakage, or spatially nonconstant lambda/S.

value.rationale: Total leakage is a practical water-budget quantity. The exact transfer function eliminates the need to solve the spatial field for this aggregate whenever the local leakage/storage timescale is uniform, even with heterogeneous transmissivity and arbitrary pumping schedules. The converse identifies when that simplification fails: a nonconstant lambda/S makes the initial aggregate leakage slope depend on source placement. This is a natural structural classification; it does not claim local-head invariance.
